changelog: v5.3 — the ladder: fill the book before flowing down. ARCHITECTURAL FIX, not a strategy lever. The cascade conflated two different situations: (1) the allocator CHOSE to be defensive — flowing down executes that decision, correct; and (2) the allocator wanted equity and a concentration control mechanically blocked the fill — flowing down there overrides the allocator with a side effect of a risk control. Case (2) is a defect. Weight freed by a concentration trim is now offered to the next-ranked ELIGIBLE-BUT-UNHELD funds in rank order, admitted only where average correlation to the post-trim book is <= max_corr 0.60 — so it cannot rebuild the cluster it just trimmed in a new ticker. Flow-down is now the EXHAUSTION path. DEFAULT ON in the engine; max_corr 0 restores the old behaviour. Motivated by a measured decomposition (scripts/probe-return-gap.ts): the equity picks BEAT SPY by +6.11pp annualised in 2021-2026 — selection is not the problem — while the defensive allocation costs -3.18pp/yr, two-thirds of it reactive overflow rather than a deliberate defensive choice, during a period that is 81% uptrends. vs v5.2: defensive weight since 2021 8.54%->2.99%, 5Y excess vs SPY +1.44->+3.94pp, RDD3y 0.060->0.026, start-cohorts-still-behind-SPY 16.77->6.78%, CAGR 18.49->18.61%, turnover UNCHANGED (4.699->4.701). Costs Martin 3.750->3.628 and worst-12mo -7.50->-7.95%: staying in equities instead of bonds earns more and tracks SPY far better, but bonds were real crash protection — 2008-09-02 is the visible case, where 7.7% moves from CASH into XPH just before the crash and loses 0.55pp. Taken because D6 ('never trail SPY for long stretches') is documented non-negotiable and audience-fatal, and Martin is an objective while D6 is a constraint. diff:engine: 29/30 scenarios identical; the one change is the new scenario 26 that exists to exercise this, and scenario 27 pins that max_corr 0 restores flow-down exactly. diff:holdings 36/247 rebalances changed. Concentration profile and stress gate unchanged.
